name: IndexedDB
plain: A large browser database that can hold gigabytes of structured data for one site.
meaning: Stores app data, offline caches and, for trackers, bigger profiles or IDs that survive cookie clearing. Quota is a share of free disk, so a site can fill hundreds of MB without a prompt.

access.persistence: Best effort: kept until the user clears it or the browser evicts under disk pressure. Safari applies the 7 day cap
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

limits.headline: Can keep gigabytes of organized data for its own site in your browser
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens as the site saves your work or caches data.
can: Store lots of structured data, such as messages, notes or a catalog
cannot: Hold more than the site's storage limit
Keep it after you clear site data
Keep it after a private window closes

story.what_it_is: A large browser database that can hold gigabytes of organized data for one site.

marketing.name: Storage for the web
marketing.pitch: Google explains IndexedDB as the main place for large offline data in web apps.

marketing.name: IndexedDB API
marketing.pitch: Documents the browser database that sites use to store large amounts of structured data.

story.for_you: You never see it. It is why a web app has your emails or notes ready offline, and why a game keeps big progress without logging in.
story.for_makers: It is the main database of the web. Makers use it for offline apps, game saves and caches. It can also hold an ID that survives clearing cookies in some cases.

use_cases.example: A browser game made with Unity or Emscripten stores its save files and downloaded levels here.
A web email or notes app keeps all your messages here for fast, offline search.
A web design tool keeps your open file safe between visits.
A web music app keeps your downloaded songs here.
A web chat app stores recent chat history for a quick start.
A tracking script keeps a hidden visitor ID here to bring you back after cookie clearing.
A web wallet or password tool keeps encrypted data here.

technical_bounds: Chrome: up to about 60% of total disk per origin
Firefox: about 10% of disk per site group, up to 10 GiB
Safari 17+: up to about 60% of disk per origin in the browser
Eviction is least recently used across origins

abuse: Cookie respawn store, large fingerprint caches

history.change: Quota model changed: per origin share of disk plus 7 day cap kept
